questions.question: Find the greatest number which divides 285 and 1249 leaving remainders 9 and 7 respectively.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number 1: 285, leaving a remainder of 9

Number 2: 1249, leaving a remainder of 7

**Formula Used:**

Greatest number which divides both numbers leaving given remainders = HCF of (Number 1 - Remainder 1) and (Number 2 - Remainder 2)

**Calculation:**

Required number = HCF of (285 - 9) and (1249 - 7)

Required number = HCF of 276 and 1242

Using the Euclidean algorithm:

1242 = 276 × 4 + 138

276 = 138 × 2 + 0

So, HCF = 138

**The greatest number which divides 285 and 1249 leaving remainders 9 and 7 respectively is 138.**

questions.question: A fort has provisions for 150 men for 45 days. After 10 days 25 men left the fort. How long will the provisions last at the same rate for the remaining men?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Provisions for 150 men for 45 days.

After 10 days, 25 men left.

**Formula Used:**

Total provisions = Number of men × Number of days

Remaining provisions = Initial provisions - Provisions used in 10 days

New number of men = Initial number of men - Number of men left

Remaining days = Remaining provisions / New number of men

**Calculation:**

Total provisions = 150 × 45

Total provisions = 6750 man-days

Provisions used in 10 days by 150 men = 150 × 10

Provisions used = 1500 man-days

Remaining provisions = 6750 - 1500

Remaining provisions = 5250 man-days

New number of men = 150 - 25

New number of men = 125 men

Remaining days = 5250 / 125

Remaining days = 42 days

**The provisions will last for 42 days.**

questions.question: 1over3 of a commodity is sold at the rate of 15% profit, 1over4 is sold at the rate of 20% profit and the rest is sold at the rate of 24% profit. If a total profit of Rs. 62 is earned, then find the cost price of the commodity.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

1/3 of a commodity is sold at the rate of 15% profit.

1/4 of the commodity is sold at the rate of 20% profit.

The rest is sold at the rate of 24% profit.

Total profit earned = Rs. 62

**Formula Used:**

Weighted Average Profit = (Sum of (Profit rate × Fraction of commodity))/Total fractions

Total Profit = (Weighted Average Profit) × (Cost Price)

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the commodity be Rs. x.

Fraction of commodity sold at 15% profit = 1/3

Fraction of commodity sold at 20% profit = 1/4

Fraction of commodity sold at 24% profit = 1 - (1/3 + 1/4)

⇒ Fraction of commodity sold at 24% profit = 1 - (4/12 + 3/12)

⇒ Fraction of commodity sold at 24% profit = 1 - 7/12

⇒ Fraction of commodity sold at 24% profit = 5/12

Weighted Average Profit = (15% × 1/3) + (20% × 1/4) + (24% × 5/12)

⇒ Weighted Average Profit = (15/100 × 1/3) + (20/100 × 1/4) + (24/100 × 5/12)

⇒ Weighted Average Profit = 5/100 + 5/100 + 10/100

⇒ Weighted Average Profit = 20/100

⇒ Weighted Average Profit = 20%

Total Profit = 20% of Cost Price

⇒ 62 = 20/100 × x

⇒ 62 = 0.2 × x

⇒ x = 62 / 0.2

⇒ x = 310

**The cost price of the commodity is Rs. 310.**

• Citrus canker is a bacterial disease caused by the bacterium Xanthomonas citri subsp. citri: 
 
• Symptoms
 
• Citrus canker causes lesions on the leaves, stems, and fruit of citrus plants. The leaves may drop and unripe fruit may fall to the ground. 
 
• Impact
 
• Citrus canker affects the health of infected citrus trees and the marketability of infected fruit. While not harmful to humans, there is no cure for citrus canker. 
 
• Spread
 
• Citrus canker is most severe in hot, wet areas. It is highly contagious and can affect all above-ground parts of citrus trees. 
 
• Control
 
 
• To control citrus canker, you can:
 
• Reduce wind speeds with windbreaks 
 
• Apply copper sprays to the fruit and leaves 
 
• Practice sanitation 
 
• Control leafminer

• Viruses can sometimes lead to chronic conditions, like HIV/AIDS.

__
 
• YOUTHSAT is an experimental satellite of the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO): 
 
• YOUTHSAT is a joint Indo-Russian mission that studies the relationship between solar variability and the thermosphere-ionosphere. 
 
• YOUTHSAT carries three payloads, two Indian and one Russian, to study the composition, energetics, and dynamics of the Earth's upper atmosphere.

• Launched on April 26, 2012.

• This helps in predicting weather changes and monitoring wind patterns over oceans.

questions.question:
Supposing that the telegraph poles on a railroad are 50 m apart, how many poles will be passed by a train in 4 h if the speed of the train is 45 km/h?

(Include both the poles at the starting point as well as the one at the end of the journey in your count)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = Speed × Time = 45 km/h × 4 h = 180 km = 1,80,000 m.

**Number of Intervals** = Total Distance ÷ Distance between poles = 1,80,000 ÷ 50 = 3600.

**Total Poles** = Number of Intervals + 1 = 3600 + 1 = 3601.

**∴ The correct answer is 3601.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total distance** covered = Speed × Time

⇒ Total distance = 45 × 4 = 180 km

⇒ Converting km to meters: 180 × 1000 = 1,80,000 m

⇒ Number of **gaps** between poles = 1,80,000 ÷ 50

⇒ Number of gaps = 3600

⇒ Since both the **starting** and **ending** poles are counted, **Total poles** = Number of gaps + 1

⇒ Total poles = 3600 + 1 = 3601

**∴ The correct answer is 3601.**

**Given:**

The broken upper part of the tree = 10 m.

Using the Pythagorean theorem for the right triangle formed:

a² + b² = c²

Where:

a = height of the tree from the break point to the ground.

b = distance from the foot of the tree to the point where the upper part touches the ground.

⇒ h² + 36 = 100

⇒ h² = 100 - 36

⇒ h² = 64

⇒ h = sqrt{64}

⇒ h = 8 meters.

The total height of the tree = height from the foot to the break point + length of the broken part.

Total height = 8 + 10 = 18 meters.

**The height of the tree is 18 meters.**

Loss percentage = 40%

Desired gain percentage = 20%

New Selling Price (SP') = CP × (1 + Gain%)

Number of rubber bands for a rupee = Total rubber bands / SP'

**Calculation:**

Given SP for 32 rubber bands = 1 rupee

Loss = 40%

⇒ New SP' = (5/3) × 1.2

⇒ New SP' = 2 rupees

Number of rubber bands for 1 rupee = 32 / New SP'

⇒ Number of rubber bands for 1 rupee = 32 / 2

15 = 15/1

Prime factors:

9 = 3²

15 = 3 × 5

Common factor: 3

LCM of 5, 20, 1 = 20

Required HCF = 3/20 = 0.15

**The HCF of 16.5, 0.45, and 15 is 0.15.**

questions.question: If the radius of a cylinder is doubled and the height is halved, what will be the ratio of the new volume to the previous volume?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **Volume** of a **cylinder** is proportional to the square of its **radius** (r²) and its **height** (h).

Change factor = (Radius change factor)² × (Height change factor)

Change factor = (2)² × (1/2) = 4 × 1/2 = 2.

Ratio of new volume to previous volume = 2 : 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **radius** = r

Initial **height** = h

New **radius** = 2r (doubled)

New **height** = h/2 (halved)

**Formula Used:**

**Volume of a cylinder** (V) = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f95067eabfdb56e7f7e3c5f399067b330372d6303652d41e568b60f770391218.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Previous **Volume** (V₁) = πr²h

⇒ New **Volume** (V₂) = π × (2r)² × (h/2)

⇒ V₂ = π × 4r² × (h/2)

⇒ V₂ = 2πr²h

⇒ Required **Ratio** = V₂ : V₁ = 2πr²h : πr²h

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 1

**∴ The correct answer is 2 : 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the curved part is given by 2 × π × r × h.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

It includes the CSA and the area of the two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same radius and height as a cylinder has (1/3) of its volume: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Volume Change Property

If **radius** is changed by a factor k and **height** by factor m, the **volume** changes by a factor k² × m.</p

questions.question: What is the sum of the measures of the interior angles of a hexagon?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The question asks for the sum of the measures of the interior angles of a hexagon.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of the interior angles of a polygon = (n - 2) × 180º, where n is the number of sides of the polygon.

**Calculation:**

For a hexagon, n = 6.

Sum of the interior angles = (6 - 2) × 180º

⇒ Sum of the interior angles = 4 × 180º

⇒ Sum of the interior angles = 720º

**The sum of the measures of the interior angles of a hexagon is 720º.**

**Given:** There are couples, Meera-Namit and Kavita-Punit. 

Let the incomes of Meera's salary, Namit's salary, Kavita's salary, and Punit's salary be M, N, K and P respectively.

Condition 1 : M + N > K + P 

2) The sum of the salaries of Meera and Kavita is the same as the sum of the salaries of Namit and Punit.

Condition 2 : M + K = N + P

3) Meera earns half as much as the sum of the salaries of Namit and punit. 

Condition 3 : 2M = N + P

Putting the value of (N + P) in condition 2, we get

M + K = N + P ⇒ M + K = 2M ⇒ K = M

Putting (K = M) in condition 1, we get

M + N > K + P ⇒ M + N > M + P ⇒ N > P

Therefore, N i.e Namit's salary is the highest.

Hence, "Option 4" is the correct answer.
